milestone: M1.5 Cross-Device Playback Progress Synchronization and Conflict Resolution

environment.postgres: 18.6; new local disposable soundwave_ci_sync_20261108 database, generated schemas and restore databases
environment.redis: 7.4.12; dedicated loopback test container and randomized prefixes
environment.browser: local headless Chrome via Playwright 1.64.1; two independent browser contexts authenticate separately
environment.installation: Existing lockfile dependencies reused; no dependencies added and npm ci was not repeated

contract.revision: starts at 0; state-changing update and explicit reset increment once; equivalent ordinary update acknowledges without another increment
contract.metadata: one latest accepted/rejected outcome per client/chapter, at most 32 newly admitted slots; historical slots retained; older sequences retired
contract.client: no blind conflict retry; Resume Latest applies paused in place; Keep My Position uses displayed revision; unknown network outcomes retry exact original request
contract.offline: public audio remains playable; no durable general offline write/event queue; current tab snapshot may retain one position

ciSafetyTests.command: node --test scripts/ci/safety.test.mjs (also executed by CI test runner)

schema.existingData: positions/completion/events/client high-water marks retained; populated fresh/reapply/import/restore tests passed

apiChanges: GET /api/progress/:chapterId returns own state, including empty revision-0 default
GET /api/progress and story chapters expose revision
PUT /api/progress/:chapterId requires expectedRevision/clientId/sequence and supports update/reset
409 includes stable code and current own state; legacy write 428; metadata admission cap 429

required: postgres: transaction rollback, concurrent completions and stale progress writes
postgres: playlist reads/writes reject anonymous sessions
Redis atomically shares request limits across independent application instances
postgres: account writes serialize concurrent field changes and roll back atomically
postgres: cross-device CAS permits one simultaneous writer and rejects stale device state
postgres: populated revision migration preserves progress, completion, events and old client high-water marks
postgres: rejected valid attempts also reserve their identity and cannot be repurposed
postgres: progress survives Redis disconnect/reconnect and streaming remains available

format.command: npm run format:check; explicit Prettier on changed docs/JSON/server package; git diff --check

findingsAndFixes: Independent client IDs previously had no shared precondition: now database CAS and durable latest outcome receipts enforce it
Valid rejected identities could be repurposed: now outcome codes reserve them transactionally
Equivalent paused saves created unnecessary revisions: no-op acknowledgements retain the revision
A saved acknowledgement could clear a later small rewind: capture local edit generations before dispatch and retain dirty state
A decision could otherwise borrow a later hidden observation: use the displayed conflict revision and show changed state before another decision
Synchronization unnecessarily reloaded media; a PostgreSQL browser run failed with a media network error. Adoption now seeks the same source paused, with a no-load unit regression
New backup child rows made fixture cleanup fail/hang: delete its progress children and always close the client
Observed local concurrent migration lock timeout: bound test files to four without changing internal simultaneous race assertions
Old tests/scripts now send explicit revisions/reset actions; stale writes that used to be ignored with 200 now assert 409
A fixture-position expectation accidentally changed during migration-count editing was restored to its original exact value 12
limitations: Current-chapter/event-driven sync only; no cross-device queue or global playback lease
Only latest outcome per admitted client/chapter is replayable; older sequences return retired conflict; 32 new client slots require existing client/operator when full
No durable general offline progress or analytics queue; cold offline bootstrap requires reload/sign-in before private sync
Concurrent streams retain existing stream-wall-time analytics; no global overlap deduplication
All old API writers must be drained for release; old browser shells must refresh (428)
Local Chrome evidence only; remote Actions, public deployment, external Google provider, full Redis-server/container crash drill and load benchmark not repeated
M1.3 general Chrome hot-cache concern remains separate and is not claimed universally fixed
